context:
Treat `surface` as visibility, `support_status` as product support level, and
`supports_dataframe` as capability. First write the policy table so tests have
a clear target. Then add metadata-only fixture tests for future statuses and
focused real-registry tests for current public beta/experimental and internal
repo_only benchmarks. Keep explicit-ID behavior stable unless the policy table
explicitly changes it.
description:
PR #502 added benchmark support status and exposed it on MCP discovery. The
immediate review follow-up fixed CLI labeling for public benchmark listings
and prevented MCP query-detail support-status leakage for internal/repo-only
benchmarks. The broader invariant still needs a durable test matrix: future
repo_only, document_only, deprecated, beta, and experimental benchmark entries
should fail loudly if a public surface exposes or hides them contrary to the
support taxonomy and `surface` policy.

Add cross-surface invariant tests and policy documentation that prove
`support_status`, `surface`, and `supports_dataframe` remain separate. The
goal is not to change visibility for current benchmarks. The goal is to make
future status additions safe and reviewable across CLI, MCP discovery, MCP
query details, docs, and result/explorer inputs where applicable.

anti_patterns.dont: build tests that depend on rich color codes
expose repo_only or document_only support claims over MCP discovery
anti_patterns.instead: omit or filter claims on explicit-ID surfaces.
anti_patterns.why: the public taxonomy says those are not MCP-exposed

anti_patterns.dont: hide all experimental benchmarks by changing support_status behavior alone
anti_patterns.instead: use explicit surface decisions for hiding.

anti_patterns.why: DataFrame support is a capability dimension

preserves.behavior: MCP discovery continues to expose support_status for public benchmarks.
Public beta and experimental benchmarks remain visible unless a separate surface/deprecation decision changes them.
joinorder_synthetic remains hidden from public discovery lists.
joinorder_synthetic remains runnable by explicit ID where it was already supported.
supports_dataframe continues to control DataFrame routing independently of support_status.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/cli/benchmarks.py: BenchmarkManager public benchmark filtering - extend tests without changing explicit-ID run behavior.
benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py:get_benchmark_support_status and get_benchmark_registry_summary - reuse for status assertions.
benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py:get_benchmark_surface and list_public_benchmark_ids - reuse for discovery visibility decisions.
benchbox/mcp/tools/benchmark.py: get_query_details benchmark_info - preserve explicit-ID compatibility while preventing unsupported support-status claims.
benchbox/mcp/tools/discovery.py: public benchmark discovery filtering - reuse as MCP listing contract.
tests/unit/core/test_registry_surface_field.py: patch.dict surface tests - reuse fixture pattern for synthetic status/surface combinations.

verifications.description: Benchmark registry and surface invariants pass.
verifications.expected: All benchmark registry and surface tests pass.

verifications.description: CLI benchmark manager support-status labeling tests pass.
verifications.expected: All selected CLI benchmark manager tests pass.
